passage:
Guests were arriving soon and Zubin was still stirring the pot. Ritu carried the spoons one at a time, laying each beside a plate. One landed on the wrong side, and she flipped it round.
"Papa, done!"
Zubin glanced over and wiped his hands. "Ritu, thank you. That was a big help. I could not have finished in time without you."
Ritu stood tall with her chin up, then straightened one more spoon that did not need it.

qa.q: What did Ritu carry to the table?
qa.a: She carried the spoons one at a time and laid each beside a plate.

qa.q: How does Ritu feel after Zubin thanks her?
qa.a: She feels important: she stands tall with her chin up and straightens another spoon.

qa.q: How does Zubin's thanks help Ritu grow?
qa.a: It names what she did and why it mattered, so she feels useful without it turning into a payment.

qa.q: How might Zubin see Ritu's spoons with guests arriving?
qa.a: He sees real help at a busy moment, since he says he could not have finished in time without her.

grounding: A parent notices the child set the table and thanks her for the big help; she feels important.

passage: In their Amman kitchen, Sami counted out five spoons, five forks and five plates. He carried them one by one to the table and put a napkin under each fork, the way Mama did. When Mama, Rania, came in with the rice, she stopped. "Sami, did you set the whole table?" He nodded. She put the pot down and looked right at him. "Thank you. That was a big help. Now I can sit down sooner." Sami sat up very straight in his chair. At dinner, Grandpa asked who set the table. Sami raised his hand before anyone could answer.

qa.q: How many plates did Sami count out?
How did Sami feel when Rania thanked him?
qa.a: He felt important and proud, sitting up very straight.

qa.q: Why did Rania's thanks work well without any reward?
qa.a: She named exactly how his help mattered, so he felt useful instead of paid.

qa.q: How might Rania feel walking in to a set table?
qa.a: She likely feels surprised and grateful that her son helped without being asked. 🙂

grounding: A young boy sets the table and his mother thanks him for a big help, making him feel important and useful without payment.

passage: Wasim's mother, Usha, was the warden at the girls' hostel. At dinner time the mess hall was busy. Wasim helped lay steel plates on the long tables, one on each mat, all the way to the end. It took ages. When Usha saw, she knelt beside him. "Wasim, you laid every plate on this table? Thank you. That saved me so much time." Wasim's chest puffed up. A big girl passing by said, "Wow, thanks, little helper!" Wasim did not ask for anything. He ran to get the water jugs too.

qa.q: What did Wasim lay on the long tables?
qa.a: He laid steel plates on the long tables.

qa.q: What does Wasim's chest puffing up suggest?
qa.a: He felt proud and important, useful because his help was noticed.

qa.q: Why was it good that Usha gave thanks and not a treat?
qa.a: Real thanks made Wasim feel useful without turning help into payment, so he wanted to keep helping.

qa.q: How might the hostel girl see Wasim's help?
qa.a: She seems amused and grateful, calling him a little helper.

grounding: A young boy lays plates in the hostel mess, and his mother thanks him warmly, making him feel important without paying him.
